nodes.question: What paper and receiving objects are visibly present in the source and edited images, and does direct feature comparison establish whether an edited receiving object is a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the images permit a grounded inventory and comparison, even if a particular identity remains unresolved. Separately report source paper and cup identification, edited paper and cup identification, and source-to-edit correspondence as established, disproved, or unresolved, with visible reasons. Inventory pass does not establish cup identity or insertion. Fail if adequate edited-image visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded inventory. A source cup does not by itself establish an edited cup, and unresolved correspondence does not prove removal.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images directly. First identify objects from visible structure in each image; then compare candidate counterparts using contour, proportions, opening or rim structure, enclosing walls, orientation, and other distinctive features that are actually visible. Allow source evidence to inform identity when supported by edited-image correspondence, but do not transfer source geometry into an occluded edit. Test retention, alteration, replacement, and unresolved correspondence without presupposing any of them. A color change alone neither establishes nor disproves cup identity. Describe edited paper boundaries, candidate receiving-object boundaries, overlap, and precisely which regions are obscured. Do not demand a visible interior as the sole identity test, infer insertion from a hand grip, or infer any object from the instruction alone.

nodes.question: Using s1's inventory, what visible boundary evidence establishes paper entry or excludes it across all relevant paper–receiver contact regions, and which specific regions remain unresolved?
nodes.criteria: Pass if a grounded boundary assessment can be reported, including unresolved relations. Fail only if adequate visibility establishes absence of the paper or any possible receiver. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded assessment. In the evidence, separately report receiver identity (cup/non-cup/unresolved), relation (entry/wholly external/rim-only/unresolved), requested progress (established/excluded/unresolved), and completion (established/excluded/unresolved). For wholly external placement, supply an exclusion certificate: identify the paper extent assessed, every relevant hidden contact region, and the affirmative geometry that excludes entry at each region. A visible foreground edge, no visible opening, or no observed disappearing segment is not by itself such a certificate. If any relevant region remains undecidable, relation is unresolved rather than wholly external. Positive requested entry requires established cup identity. Conversely, entry excluded into every candidate receiver establishes no requested insertion progress even if receiver identity is unresolved. Mapping success itself earns no progress or completion credit.
nodes.binding: Consume s1 as coarse ancestor context, then inspect the edited image directly. Map visible paper edges and candidate receiver boundaries with relative locations, overlap ordering, and the scope of each observation. For each hidden paper segment, identify its occluder and visible endpoints where available. Distinguish an occluded paper edge from a receiver surface or possible opening hidden behind the paper. When considering wholly external placement, test whether the stated evidence excludes entry anywhere relevant, rather than merely showing one exposed region in front. When considering unresolved entry, name the actual localized ambiguity and explain why visible geometry does not settle it; do not rely on generic hand occlusion or purely imagined hidden geometry. Report missing exclusion evidence honestly without inventing an entry path. Assess curved lines from visible structure without presuming they are rims or markings. Do not assume colors, source correspondence, or cup identity. Return the boundary assessment, exclusion certificate or its specific evidentiary gap, and separately typed findings as evidence within the saved checker response format.

nodes.question: Does direct inspection establish completed paper stuffing into a cup, affirmative incompleteness with established progress, affirmative exclusion of requested progress, or unresolved extent?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when edited paper-and-cup identity, positive entry, and visible containment or compression establish completed stuffing; exposed paper is compatible with completion. Fail when affirmative evidence establishes incomplete stuffing, wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing progress, or absence of a required object. Separately report progress as established, excluded, or unresolved and completion as established, excluded, or unresolved. Unknown when completion depends on unresolved identity or geometry, or established entry cannot be distinguished as intermediate versus completed stuffing. A fail with established progress can support partial; a fail supports absent only with affirmative exclusion of progress. A global external-placement finding must meet the nested check's exclusion certificate, not merely repeat its conclusion. Unresolved receiver identity does not prevent exclusion if geometry establishes no entry into any candidate receiver. Missing positive cues cannot establish that exclusion.
nodes.binding: Read s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order, using their evidence and typed findings rather than execution statuses. Inspect the edited image directly to adjudicate stuffing extent. For a claimed global exclusion, revisit each relevant hidden contact region and explain whether the nested exclusion certificate is supported, contradicted, or incomplete. For a claimed ambiguity, identify the specific unresolved region and whether direct inspection settles it. Record any grounded correction to ancestor findings and its visual reason; dependent repetition is not independent confirmation. Do not transfer source cup geometry to an occluded edited object or infer entry from the hand grip. Keep positive insertion progress separate from mere object appearance changes. Return only pass/fail/unknown as status; describe progress, completion, and reconciliation in evidence. Invalid observations, schema errors, and transport failures are unavailable evidence, not proof of no progress.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in saved order. Interpret evidence and separately typed findings, not support status alone. Complete requires established edited paper-and-cup identity, positive cup entry, and established completed stuffing from s2. Partial requires positively established requested insertion or intermediate stuffing into an established cup and affirmative incompleteness from s2. Absent requires affirmative exclusion of requested progress: adequately visible required-object absence, established rim-only placement without stuffing progress, or wholly external placement supported by the nested exclusion certificate and explicitly assessed by s2. A wholly external label accompanied only by local foreground overlap or missing entry cues is insufficient. Receiver identity uncertainty does not block absent when grounded geometry excludes entry into every candidate receiver, but it cannot itself provide that exclusion. Unknown applies when any necessary fact remains unresolved, a required observation is unavailable or invalid, or conflicting findings lack evidence-based reconciliation. A grounded correction by s2 may resolve a conflict only through its stated visible reasons; repetition does not constitute independent confirmation. Inventory and mapping passes earn no requested completion credit. Failure to establish completion or entry does not establish no progress. Infer no new visual facts and do not treat execution or transport failures as visual negatives.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
